title: King moves on ANY hidden grid: exact backtracking over the clue letters for a free arrangement of the 26 letters, widths 3-13, 26 or 27 cells, flat / column wrap / both wrap; feasibility and fewest different moves
k4_result: A grid exists on 58 of the 66 grid shapes (0 undecided). Impossible for ANY arrangement on 8 shapes: width 12 flat (26 and 27 cells) and width 13 in all three conventions (26 and 27 cells). Fewest different moves D (stay counted): 4 on 35 shapes (widths 4-7 in every convention; widths 3 and 8-11 only with wraps), 5 on the other 23. D = 4 equals the lower bound the pairs force without any grid (T goes to three different cipher letters, plus the stays S->S and K->K). The grids are far from unique: at the smallest D there are 8 to more than 20,000 placements of the 21 clue letters per shape (fewest: 26 cells w12 column wrap 8, w7 flat 40), and more than 20,000 without a limit on D on every feasible shape; the 5 non-clue letters are free on top. Nothing can be decrypted from this.
controls: 200 shuffled K4s, same code. Feasible shapes: min 17, median 55, max 66; 65 of 200 (32.5%) have at least K4's 58. Smallest D on any shape: 3 in 9 shuffles, 4 in 85, 5 in 88, 6 in 18; 94 of 200 (47%) are at or below K4's 4. Shapes with D <= 4: mean 11.6, max 66; 31 of 200 (15.5%) have at least K4's 35. Smallest D minus the lower bound: 0 in 65, 1 in 113, 2 in 21, 3 in 1 (K4 0; 32.5% as good). K4's many D = 4 shapes come from its clue graph having only 1 closed ring (21 letters, 21 different pairs, because R->P repeats and two letters stay): the 10 shuffles with 1 ring average 36.0 shapes at their lower bound (K4 35), those with 2 rings 19.7, 3 rings 4.2. The 8 shapes impossible for K4 are also the hardest for shuffles (impossible for 132-177 of 200). 43 shuffles have 1-9 undecided shapes (node limit), mostly width 3 and 9-12 with wraps; 3-47 of 200 smallest-D values per shape are upper ends only.
planted: 11/11: English texts moved by random king moves on random hidden grids (8 with any move: w5, w7, w4, w13 flat 26 cells, w9 and w3 flat 27 cells, w6 column wrap, w7 both wraps; 3 with only 3-4 allowed moves). Each came out feasible, the true grid passed the separate check, the smallest D found was never above the true grid's (3 and 4 found exactly for the fixed-move plants), and with 7 letters freed the complete list of solutions (46-2,220 grids) held the true grid. 0 of all placements found in the run failed the separate check.
scope_limits: Feasible is not a decryption: the grid and the key are both free, so no text was produced and nothing was scored as English. One grid used for both plain and cipher letters; moves of exactly one cell or a stay; rows of one width with a short last row; with 27 cells one empty cell anywhere (a letter may not step onto it); wrap rules as in idea 123. Not covered: a separate cipher grid, moves of two or more cells, knight or other moves, non-rectangular layouts, 28+ cells, widths 2 and 14+. The count of grids is of clue-letter placements, capped at 20,000 and not reduced by symmetry. Smallest D is exact for K4 on all 58 shapes; for some shuffles it is an upper end only.

negative.family: compass steps on a letter grid (free hidden grid)
negative.hypothesis: Some hand-made arrangement of the 26 letters in a grid makes every one of the 24 clue pairs a king move or a stay, and the clues pin that grid down or at least set K4 apart from shuffled text.
negative.scope: Every arrangement of the 26 letters (exact backtracking over the 21 clue letters) on grids of width 3-13 with 26 or 27 cells, flat / columns wrap / both wrap (66 shapes); one grid for plain and cipher; fewest different moves searched upward from an exact lower bound.
negative.outcome: No signal: a grid exists on 58 of 66 shapes, with thousands of grids each and as few as 4 different moves on 35 shapes, so the clues do not constrain a free grid. Dead for any arrangement only on width 12 flat and width 13 (8 shapes). Controls: 200 shuffled K4s, feasible shapes median 55 (32.5% >= K4), smallest D <= 4 in 47%, 35+ shapes at D <= 4 in 15.5%, and shuffles with one ring like K4 average 36 shapes at their lower bound. Planted 11/11 feasible with the true grid listed.

follow_ups: Few-move version with a reading: on K4's D = 4 grids each cipher letter has at most 4 plain candidates (itself or one of 3 fixed steps back). For the tightest shapes (w7 flat 40 placements, w4 flat 104, w5 flat 120, w12 column wrap at D = 5: 8) enumerate every placement, try every position of the 5 free letters, decode with the quadgram Viterbi of idea 123 and compare with the same on shuffled K4s.

Same solver with a rule on the key instead of a free key: the move repeats with a period, or follows the words EAST / NORTHEAST letter by letter; this turns the tree-like clue graph into real ring constraints and may be decidable where the free key is not.
